messages:

To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot ask - sub-90ms P95 for Q1 pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the throughput and the routing features. We're gearing up for a paid pilot in Q1 and I need to check a hard constraint from our product team: they want a short-term commitment to a sub-90ms P95 for inference during pilot hours (8am-8pm PST) for up to 500 concurrent users.

I realize this is tighter than your standard public SLOs. Can Redwood commit to a temporary, measured exception for the pilot, with the understanding we will be on a Dedicated pool or private deployment? If so, our legal team will draft the minimal language and we can add telemetries to the MAP.

I've attached our internal benchmark that drove the ask and a draft MAP. Happy to jump on a call if useful.

Best,
Priya

Marissa — thanks for flagging this. Quick assessment from Product/Infra:

1) Feasibility: Technically achievable in Dedicated for short windows with the right config (pinned model variant, reduced sequence length, quantization profile tuned for latency). The biggest risk is noisy neighbor behavior at 500 concurrent — we'd want a dedicated GPU pool sized for sustained concurrency (estimate: 4x A100-equivalent workers during pilot hours).

2) Conditions we should require for a time-limited SLA exception:
- Customer must run on Redwood Dedicated (or Private) with reserved capacity.
- Agreed operational hours (8am-8pm PST) and a monitoring dashboard sharing token-level latency.
- Failure/rollback policy: automatic fallback to a less aggressive quantized model and a clear threshold where we remove the exception (e.g., sustained P95 > 120ms for 30 minutes).
- A brief onboarding spike test week (2 days) to size pools before the pilot starts.

3) Metrics & telemetry: We'll want packet-level traces, token timing, and sampling of model runtimes. We can provide a dashboard and an alert for P95 > 100ms.

4) Operational cost: This will materially increase unit cost during pilot hours. Sales should expect an uplift in the pricing for the Dedicated pool or an interim pilot surcharge. Finance needs to sign off if we offer credits.

If you want, Ops (Tessa) can attach a short runbook and SRE sign-off language. My recommendation: provisional approval subject to (a) Dedicated pool commit and (b) 2-day sizing test. If legal wants exact wording I'll work with you on a narrow clause.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, SentryWorks Legal <legal@sentryworks.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot ask - sub-90ms P95 for Q1 pilot

Thanks — quick ops take and proposed wording for a provisional email we can send to Priya and Legal. Ops has reviewed the attachments and run the sample traces. We can support a time-limited exception with the following operational commitments and exit criteria.

Provisional commitment (example language):
"Redwood Inference will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain a P95 inference latency <= 90 milliseconds during the agreed pilot hours (8:00–20:00 PST) for the duration of the pilot, conditional on SentryWorks running on a Dedicated Redwood pool with reserved capacity, completion of a 2-day sizing validation, and adherence to the operational runbook. The parties agree that unexpected infra events or customer-controlled load spikes may require temporary fallback to a higher-latency configuration; Redwood will notify SentryWorks and remediate per the runbook."

Exit / rollback criteria (Ops):
- Sustained P95 > 120ms for 30 minutes triggers automatic rollback to the fall-back model and temporary suspension of the sub-90ms commitment until investigation completes.
- Any critical infra incident (severity 1) during pilot hours nullifies the exception for the affected window.

Next steps I need from Sales/Legal:
- Sales to confirm pricing uplift or pilot surcharge to cover reserved Dedicated pool.
- Legal to provide minimal clause language and confirm acceptability of the rollback triggers.
- Marissa: confirm you want me to send this note to Priya + CC Legal, or do you want to iterate first?

I'll attach a 1-page runbook and a short checklist (sizing inputs, alert thresholds, contact rotas).

-Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Site Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com
